content.comment_body: Hello, I currently have this setup: - 2x [company_name] [product_name]; - 2x Mean Well Power Supply HDR-150-24; Each controller has its own power supply (PS1-CPU1 / PS2-CPU2). My question is: - Is it possible to use a single return (ground) signal from one power supply to trigger inputs on both controllers? - I tried connecting both power supplies' grounds together, and I could trigger one controller's input using the Vcc signal from the other power supply. The power supplies also provide power to different loads, such as LED lighting. Is this configuration safe, or am I missing something that could cause issues over time? Thank you very much for your help and advice! Best Regards, [user_name]

I'm not sure what you mean by "return signal." You can connect the 0V (or M) terminal of both power supplies together; this will not cause any harm. Both controllers will then share the same electrical potential.
In electronics, the term "return signal" often refers to "signal ground," which is the M terminal on power supplies. The signal current flows back to the supply through this point.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are clarifying the connections of grounds between two [company_name] controller modules powered by separate power supplies, with focus on safety and reliability. The term 'return signal' caused some confusion, but users agreed that joining power supply grounds is a standard practice to ensure common potential. analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to safely connect the grounds of two separate power supplies and utilize a shared signal return for controller inputs, wanting reassurance that this approach is common and does not present safety or reliability concerns.
